pacing_and_device_recommendations.temporary_pacing: Recommended in cases of failure to respond to atropine (Class I, Level C).
pacing_and_device_recommendations.urgent_angiography: Recommended with a view to revascularization if the patient has not received previous reperfusion therapy (Class I, Level C).
pacing_and_device_recommendations.permanent_pacemaker: Implantation recommended when high-degree AV block does not resolve within a waiting period of at least 5 days after MI (Class I, Level C).
pacing_and_device_recommendations.early_CRT_consideration: In selected patients with high-degree AV block in the context of an anterior wall MI and acute HF, early device implantation (CRT-D/CRT-P) may be considered (Class IIb, Level C).
pacing_and_device_recommendations.pacing_not_recommended: Pacing is not recommended if high-degree AV block resolves after revascularization or spontaneously (Class III, Level B).

abbreviations_and_terms.list_summary: Abbreviations listed include ACS, AF, AV, CHA2DS2-VASc, Congestive heart failure, Hypertension, Diabetes, CKD, CMR, CRT-D/CRT-P, HAS-BLED, HF, IABP, ICD, LV, LVEF, MI, NOAC, NYHA, STEMI, VF, VKA, VT, among others.
abbreviations_and_terms.note: Class of recommendation and level of evidence annotations appear alongside recommendations.

12.3_comorbid_conditions.12.3.1_heading: Patients at high bleeding risk and with blood disorders (anaemia and thrombocytopaenia)
12.3_comorbid_conditions.anaemia_prevalence_and_associations: Anaemia is more prevalent in elderly/frail ACS patients and in patients with multimorbidity (eg, heart failure, chronic kidney disease, diabetes mellitus, cancer, autoimmune diseases). Severe anaemia may precipitate Type 2 MI.
12.3_comorbid_conditions.clinical_implications: Persistent or worsening anaemia in patients with ACS is associated with increased risk of recurrent ischaemic events, death, and major bleeding.
12.3_comorbid_conditions.haemoglobin_thresholds_for_HBR: According to ARC-HBR, haemoglobin <11 g/dL at the time of PCI constitutes a major criterion for high bleeding risk (HBR). Haemoglobin between 11 and 13 g/dL (12 g/dL for women) is a minor criterion.
